title: Geostatistical Determination of Radiation Dosimetry Maps of Population Exposures
author: Eliseos Mucaki
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba4nigve

Create a Union of the two polygons;

steps.title: Prepare HPAC Plume Data
steps.instruction: Convert HPAC plume XML files (containing WGS1984 coordinates and dose values in cGy) into a tab-delimited X,Y,Z format (Latitude, Longitude, Dose).

substeps.instruction: Use the Perl script 'XML-to-XY-Converter.Smooth-Circle-of-Zeros.All-Files.pl' to perform the conversion.
Ensure the script adds a '0 cGy' unirradiated contour surrounding the plume to serve as the geographic boundary for kriging.

steps.title: Acquire and Process Boundary Files
steps.instruction: Download and prepare US state and sub-division boundary files for the region of interest.

substeps.instruction: Download KML boundary files from the US census bureau (https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2016/shp/).
Determine population of regions using US Census, American Fact Finder, or Home Town Locator.
Run the Perl script 'KML-Name-Correcting-Program.pl' to handle duplicate sub-division names and concatenate names with spaces or dashes.
Import modified KML files into ArcMap using the 'KMLtoLayer' tool.

Use the 'Split' command in ArcMap to identify individual sub-divisions: set 'Input Features' and 'Split Features' to the KML file, 'Split Field' to 'Name', and create a new Geodatabase (e.g., 'StateName_Split') as the 'Target Workspace'.

steps.title: Generate Random Sampling Locations
steps.instruction: Create a set of random points to simulate sampling 0.1% of the population in each geographic sub-division overlapping the plume.

substeps.instruction: Upload HPAC plume files to ArcMap to visually identify overlapping sub-divisions.
Execute a Python script using 'arcpy.CreateRandomPoints_management' to generate points for each sub-division (number of points = 0.1% of sub-division population).
Merge random points into a single file using 'arcpy.Merge_management'.
Add XY coordinates using 'arcpy.AddXY_management'.
Run the script in ArcMap via Geoprocessing -> Python (execfile). If ArcMap crashes, process in batches of 10-25 cycles.
Export the random sample locations to a text file using the 'Random-Point-Exporting-Script.py' script.

steps.title: Assign Radiation Dose Values
steps.instruction: Assign simulated radiation dose values to the sampling locations based on the HPAC plume data.

substeps.instruction: Run the Perl script 'XML-to-XY-Conversion.REM-Assigner.Multiple-Files.pl'.
Edit the script to specify the full path to the HPAC plume file ($filename) and the folder containing exported random point files ($randompointspath).
The script will assign values in cGy; locations not overlapping the plume are assigned 0 cGy.

steps.title: Generate Radiation Plume via Kriging
steps.instruction: Create a radiation exposure map using Empirical Bayesian Kriging (EBK) in ArcMap.

substeps.instruction: Import point data via 'Add Data' and use 'Display XY Data' (X: Longitude, Y: Latitude, Z: Data; Spatial Reference: WGS 1984).
Open the Geostatistical Wizard and select 'Empirical Bayesian Kriging'.
Set the Source Dataset to the imported event and the Data Field to 'Data' (or field 3), using default values for analysis.
Double-click the resulting intermediate plume, go to 'Symbology' -> 'Classify', select 'Equal Intervals', and set classes to 7 (ranges of 0-100, 100-200... 600-700 cGy).
Set the 0-100 cGy symbol to 'No Color'.

steps.title: Densify Sampling Network
steps.instruction: Identify high-variance regions to optimize subsequent sampling and improve map accuracy.

substeps.instruction: In the Geostatistical Toolbox, select 'Densify Sampling Network'.
Set 'Input Geostatistical Layer' to the kriging plume, 'Number of output points' to 200, 'Selection Criteria' to 'QUARTILE_THRESHOLD_UPPER', and 'Threshold Value' to 200 (cGy).
Optional: Set an inhibition distance of 1 meter.
Use 'Add XY Coordinates' (Data Management toolbox) on the output points.
Export the result as a text file via the Attributes Table (Export -> Text File).

steps.title: Iterate Plume Refinement
steps.instruction: Repeat the sampling and kriging process iteratively until the plume converges.

substeps.instruction: Assign radiation values to densification points using the process in the 'Assign Radiation Dose Values' step.
Combine new sampling locations with all previous sample files.
Regenerate the plume using the 'Generate Radiation Plume via Kriging' step.
Repeat the Densify -> Assign -> Combine -> Kriging cycle until the plume is no longer significantly different from the previous iteration.

steps.title: Compare and Validate Plumes
steps.instruction: Quantify the overlap and accuracy of the derived plume against previous iterations or the original HPAC plume.

substeps.instruction: Generate kriging layers for comparison with identical classification ranges.
Use 'GA Contour to Layer' (Contour Type: SAME_AS_LAYER, Classification: Equal Interval) for both layers.
Convert contours to polygons using 'Feature To Polygon'.
Manually add radiation values back to the polygon attribute tables if lost.
Perform a 'Union' (Geoprocessing -> Union) of the two polygons and export the attribute table to Excel.
For iteration comparison: Sum 'Shape_Area' of matching vs non-matching radiation levels; discontinue iterations if agreement exceeds 90%.
For HPAC accuracy: Sum 'Shape_Area' of overlapping regions ≥ 2Gy and divide by the total 'Shape_Area' of the HPAC plume regions ≥ 2Gy.
